query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding a specific concentration of titanium dioxide (TiO2) to silica (SiO2) will enhance the glass-forming ability of the resulting glass.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of titanium dioxide (TiO2) into the silica matrix.
generation.conditions: Controlled melting temperature and time during the glass formation process.
generation.structural_mediator: The presence of TiO2 modifies the network structure of silica, potentially increasing the connectivity and reducing the viscosity.
generation.mechanism: TiO2 acts as a network former, which can enhance the glass-forming ability by improving the stability of the glass network and lowering the melting temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: The glass formed with TiO2 will have a lower melting temperature and improved glass-forming ability compared to pure silica.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the specific concentration range of TiO2 that is effective in enhancing glass-forming ability.
generation.uncertainty: The exact concentration of TiO2 that maximizes the glass-forming ability is uncertain and may vary based on other compositional factors.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of experiments where varying concentrations of TiO2 are added to SiO2, and the melting temperatures and glass-forming abilities are measured.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of TiO2 does not lower the melting temperature or improve the glass-forming ability compared to pure SiO2, the hypothesis will be falsified.
